stories.title: Mount Etna Absolute Gravimetry Dataset: 19 Years of Measurements (2007-2025)
stories.description: This Data Descriptor presents a curated dataset of absolute gravity measurements collected at Mount Etna between 2007 and 2025, providing a 19-year record of gravity changes across one of the most active volcanic systems worldwide. The dataset comprises repeated observations at 13 benchmarks spanning summit, upper flank, and peripheral sectors, enabling the investigation of gravity changes over multiple spatial and temporal scales. Combined with complementary relative gravity observations, the dataset provides a high-quality reference for volcano monitoring, time-series analyses, geophysical model calibration, inversion studies, and integration with deformation, seismic, and geochemical observations. This openly available dataset represents one of the longest continuous absolute gravity records acquired at an active volcano and provides a valuable resource for investigating subsurface mass redistribution associated with volcanic activity.

stories.title: Energy efficient and reliable routing in underwater internet of things using grid based fuzzy logic and multi hop forwarding
stories.description: Energy efficiency and reliable communication are persistent challenges in underwater Internet of Things (UIoT) sensor networks due to limited resources and variable underwater acoustic conditions. Efficient routing is therefore needed to overcome these challenges and ensure reliable, long-term underwater monitoring. In this paper, an energy-efficient and scalable routing system for underwater networks is proposed, called the Grid-Based Fuzzy Logic Optimal Routing Protocol (GFLORP). The proposed protocol divides the underwater monitoring region into logical blocks and establishes a grid-based layout, enabling organized communication and localized coordination. A fuzzy inference system is used to select cluster heads considering residual energy, link quality, and node degree. To ensure reliable data delivery to the sink, it employs a multi-hop forwarding technique. The simulation results show that GFLORP outperforms the existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of network lifetime, energy consumption, packet delivery ratio, and end-to-end delay. The results show that GFLORP performs well in both sparse and dense deployment scenarios, making it a suitable protocol for dynamic and scalable underwater IoT ecosystems.

stories.title: An integrated dataset of clinopyroxene-melt and amphibole-melt cation partitioning in hydrous alkaline primitive to intermediate magmas
stories.description: Trace element partitioning in clinopyroxene and amphibole governs the geochemical evolution of alkaline magmas, directly impacting liquid lines of descent reconstruction, volcanic hazard assessment and magmatic ore exploration in these volcanic settings. However, predictive models for these complex mineral phases remain limited by a lack of experimental data constraining the effects of intensive and extensive thermodynamic properties on cation substitutions in coexisting amphibole-clinopyroxene crystals. To expand this knowledge base, we present a dataset of clinopyroxene-melt and amphibole-melt partition coefficients. Piston cylinder experiments utilized natural alkali basalt and mugearite starting compositions, with starting H2O contents ranging between 3.7 and 7 wt.%, and T comprised between 1100 °C and 975 °C. The coexistence of both mineral phases in all the experiments allowed us to derive a set of clinopyroxene-melt and amphibole-melt partition coefficients especially important when interpreting amphibole-clinopyroxene parageneses in alkaline magmas. Furthermore, by employing the lattice strain formalism and an iterative numerical approach, it was possible to provide additional constraints to partitioning results, further validating the dataset. This validated dataset provides the empirical foundation for predictive partitioning models, necessary for modeling magma differentiation and dynamics in both active and quiescent alkaline plumbing systems.

stories.title: Rare cancer incidence and mortality trends among older adults in Martinique: a population-based registry study, 2008-2022
stories.description: Rare cancers account for approximately 25% of all cancers worldwide, and around 50% of cancer cases occur in people aged ≥ 65 years. However, they remain underrepresented in epidemiological research, particularly in the Caribbean. We conducted a population-based cohort study using data from the Martinique Cancer Registry and French National Mortality Database. Age-standardized incidence and mortality rates (ASIR and ASMR) were estimated, and Annual Percent Change (APC) were calculated for patients aged ≥ 65 years by tumor site and sex. Between 2008 and 2022, 778 older adults were diagnosed with rare cancers in Martinique (61% men), with 442 deaths recorded (64.5% men). Overall incidence and mortality showed no statistically significant trends in either sex (men: APC for mortality was +0.23%, 95% CI −2.46 to 2.99, p = 0.869). Significant trend was rising gallbladder cancer mortality in men (APC + 10.35%; 95% CI 1.99–19.38; p = 0.014). The mortality burden was predominant in men for laryngeal cancer (86.1%), melanoma of the skin (81.8%), and esophageal cancer (77.6%). Rare cancer patterns in older adults in Martinique reflect tumor biology, demographic aging, and healthcare constraints. Rare cancer mortality underscores critical gaps in access and timely oncological referral. Strengthening cancer registries are essential to inform Caribbean evidence-based rare cancer control.

stories.title: Tumor genomic alterations and their exploratory association with treatment response in recurrent head and neck cancer patients
stories.description: While the genetic landscape of treatment-naïve head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is well characterized, the molecular features of recurrent disease remain less defined. We investigated the genetic alterations in recurrent HNSCC and their associations with overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), and treatment response. We performed a retrospective analysis of 86 patients with recurrent HNSCC treated at the University of Maryland Medical Center. Clinical data were extracted from electronic health records, and targeted DNA sequencing of tumor samples was performed by Tempus. Genomic profiles were compared with primary HNSCC profiles from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA). Associations between mutations and clinical outcomes were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models. TP53 mutations were most prevalent (55%) and significantly correlated with worse OS (HR: 1.77, p = 0.033) and poor treatment response (p = 0.0067). CDKN2A (29%) and TERT (26%) mutations occurred more frequently in recurrent tumors compared to primary TCGA tumors. While CDKN2A mutations showed better PFS (HR: 0.57, p = 0.045), TERT mutations showed association with poorer PFS (HR: 1.66, p = 0.045) and reduced response to immune therapy (p = 0.0854), although the latter did not reach statistical significance. Notably, although in small number, FGF4 (9%) mutations were associated with significantly poor survival (HR: 2.16, p = 0.049) and poorer outcomes following surgery and/or radiotherapy (p = 0.0124). However, contradictory to other mutated genes, PIK3CA mutations (14%) correlated with better OS (HR: 0.37, p = 0.032). Recurrent HNSCC exhibit distinct genomic alterations associated with survival and therapeutic response. These findings are exploratory and hypothesis-generating. Prospective validation in larger, independent cohorts is necessary before these associations can inform treatment decisions.

stories.title: The developers have made DLSS 5 less resource-intensive and doubled the FPS • Межа
stories.description: A community of modders has drastically increased frame rates in games using NVIDIA DLSS 5 without installing a second graphics card. They managed to get the technology to work before frame upscaling, rather than after.
